_meta.title: Hand-checked facts that the Alberta jurisdiction CSV adds to the machine-read inputs
_meta.rule: Every entry names the page or document it was read from. status is VERIFIED only where the words were read in the fetched file; otherwise UNVERIFIED.
_meta.note: Municipal web addresses move often. Four municipal PDF links found by search returned HTTP 404 when fetched on 2026-10-29 (Lethbridge request-for-specific-variance PDF, Rocky View County Alternative-Solution-Proposal.pdf at the old path, Red Deer 2025 building permit form, Lethbridge bylaw 6110 on the govstack host).

default_building_ahj_asca: Alberta Safety Codes Authority (ASCA); the owner chooses one of the ASCA-contracted agencies

0159.ahj: Parks Canada (Waterton Lakes National Park townsite and park)
0159.note: Parks Canada page: "Parks Canada regulates all planning and development in the townsite and across Waterton Lakes National Park." Its Land Use Planning Regulations replaced the National Parks Building Regulations.

0164.ahj: Parks Canada (Banff National Park outside the Town of Banff; Lake Louise area is run by the Lake Louise, Yoho and Kootenay field unit)
0164.note: Parks Canada page: "This information is not applicable within the Town of Banff." Building permits in the park are issued by Parks Canada to check compliance with national and provincial codes.

0167.ahj: Parks Canada (Jasper National Park, including the Town of Jasper townsite)
0167.note: Parks Canada page: "A Building Permit is required when a proposed development contains life-safety elements covered under the National Building Code - Alberta Edition." Parks Canada publishes an Authorized Accredited Safety Code Agencies list (PDF).

0168.status: VERIFIED for the national rule; UNVERIFIED for a park-specific page
0168.note: No Elk Island permit page was fetched. The National Parks of Canada Land Use Planning Regulations (SOR/2024-230) apply to all national parks. Parks Canada's national page says: "Most construction and development activities in national parks and national park reserves require permits issued under the authority of the Land Use Planning Regulations", with a development permit first and then a building permit "if required".

0179.ahj: Parks Canada (Wood Buffalo National Park, Alberta part), by the name of the improvement district only
0179.status: VERIFIED for the national rule; UNVERIFIED for a park-specific page
0179.note: The MAPL names this improvement district Wood Buffalo and gives it 706 people. No Wood Buffalo National Park permit page was fetched, and the link between the district and the park was not checked against a boundary file. Parks Canada's national page says: "Most construction and development activities in national parks and national park reserves require permits issued under the authority of the Land Use Planning Regulations", with a development permit first and then a building permit "if required".

0479.note: Improvement District No. 25 (Willmore Wilderness) has no SCC accreditation. Willmore Wilderness is a provincial wilderness park by name; no permit page was fetched. Default ASCA routing is the Order's rule for areas with no accredited organization.

0206.ahj: City of Lloydminster (Alberta part) under the Lloydminster Charter and Building Bylaw 59-2011 for building; gas and electrical go to ASCA for Alberta properties
0206.status: VERIFIED for the split; UNVERIFIED for the code edition
0206.note: City page: "Contact Alberta Safety Codes Authority (ASCA) for properties in Alberta and Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK) for properties in Saskatchewan" for gas and electrical. Charter s.51 lets Council declare an edition of the National Building Code in force by bylaw. The Charter text has no mention of the Safety Codes Act. Bylaw 59-2011 is an image-only PDF and could not be read. SCC lists no accreditation for the City. Table C-2 of NBC(AE) lists Lloydminster.

0418.ahj: Parks Canada issues the building permit in the Jasper townsite; the Municipality of Jasper is accredited for Fire only (M000461)
0418.note: Parks Canada Jasper page requires a Parks Canada Building Permit when life-safety elements are covered by the NBC(AE); the Municipality reviews development files for municipal requirements.

0387.note: Town of Banff is accredited for Building and Fire (M000396). Parks Canada's Banff page excludes the Town from its own development permit information.

0373.note: Kananaskis Improvement District is accredited for Building, Electrical, Fire, Gas and Plumbing (M000202). It is the only improvement district with an accreditation.

first_nations.default_ahj: First Nation council by-law (Indian Act s.81(1)(h)) or land code; not an SCC-accredited organization under its own name
first_nations.default_note: SCC name search on 2026-10-29 found no accredited organization under any of the 48 First Nation names (only unrelated municipalities such as Beaver County, City of Cold Lake and County of St. Paul matched substrings). Indian Act s.81(1)(h) lets a band council make by-laws on the regulation of the construction, repair and use of buildings. Whether a Nation adopts the NBC(AE), the NBC or its own code is set by the Nation. The Safety Codes Act defines person to include a band (s.1(1)(w)) but does not itself say it applies on reserves.
first_nations.default_status: INFERENCE for the AHJ kind (Indian Act s.81(1)(h) power plus no SCC accreditation under any of the 48 names); VERIFIED for the Indian Act text and for the SCC search result; UNVERIFIED for how the Safety Codes Act applies on reserves

0448.service_provider: Superior Safety Codes (electrical, plumbing and gas permits on the Taza designated lands, per the Nation's law)
0448.note: Tsuut'ina Nation publishes the Taza Development Building Regulations Law, 2019. It defines Building Code as the National Building Code at the time of construction unless a Provincial or Tsuut'ina Nation code is more stringent, names a Nation Building Inspector, and says electrical, plumbing and gas permits "will be issued by Superior Safety Codes".

0426.note: Enoch Cree Nation Zoning Bylaw No. 2018-01 says it is "enacted pursuant to sections 81(1)(g)(h) of the Indian Act"; its Land Use Bylaw refers to the Enoch Cree Nation Building Bylaw No. 2018-01 and says attached suites "must meet Alberta Building Code requirements". The Building Bylaw text was not read.
0426.status: VERIFIED for the zoning bylaw; UNVERIFIED for the building bylaw

0419.note: The City of Calgary newsroom (18 June 2019) reports a Siksika Nation Safety Codes Officer Program with Alberta Municipal Affairs and the City of Calgary; a mentor said that by training its own officers Siksika Nation "can become accredited as Authority Having Jurisdiction". No later accreditation was found.

metis_settlements.note_accredited: Settlement is an accredited municipality for Building under the Safety Codes Act definition that municipality includes a Metis settlement (s.1(1)(u)).
metis_settlements.note_unaccredited: Settlement has no SCC accreditation; Building goes to ASCA.
metis_settlements.source: https://www.qp.alberta.ca/documents/Acts/S01.pdf ; https://www.qp.alberta.ca/documents/Acts/M14.pdf ; https://www.qp.alberta.ca/documents/Regs/2016_029.pdf ; SCC Accreditation Search name queries of 2026-10-29
metis_settlements.legal_basis: Safety Codes Act s.1(1)(u): municipality includes, for the purposes of this Act, a Metis settlement; s.1(1)(r)(ii): local authority includes, for the purposes of this Act, a settlement council of a Metis settlement. The Metis Settlements Act (RSA 2000 c M-14, sha256 423ef50c...7144) has no reference to the Safety Codes Act. A settlement without an accreditation falls under AR 29/2016 s.4(1) (ASCA).

extra_rows.legal_name: Calgary International Airport lands (Calgary Airport Authority)
extra_rows.building_ahj: City of Calgary issues the building permit; the Calgary Airport Authority authorizes the project first (Construction and Installation Permit)
extra_rows.note: YYC CIP Manual, Land Projects (December 2024): "Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) for reviewing building code compliance for projects on YYC airport lands is the City of Calgary." The municipalities will not accept an application without a letter of authorization from the Authority.

extra_rows.building_ahj: Rocky View County issues the building permit; the Calgary Airport Authority authorizes the project first
extra_rows.note: Same manual: "For all projects at Springbank Airport, the AHJ is Rocky View County."

extra_rows.legal_name: Edmonton International Airport lands (Edmonton Regional Airports Authority)
extra_rows.building_ahj: Leduc County is the primary AHJ for Alberta Safety Code items; the airport operator runs its own project approval first
extra_rows.status: VERIFIED for the airport's statement; UNVERIFIED that every parcel is under Leduc County
extra_rows.note: Edmonton Airports 2026 contractor form (FAP): "I am aware that Leduc County is the primary Authority Having Jurisdiction for Edmonton International Airport for items related to the Alberta Safety Code." and "All other fees for Alberta Safety Code permits will be paid directly to Leduc County as the Authority Having Jurisdiction". A search summary says some nearby projects list City of Edmonton permits, so confirm by parcel.

ais_stakeholder.note: Listed by the MAPL as a stakeholder type, not a municipality. No SCC accreditation under this name was searched. Building AHJ not determined.
